episodes.173216: Marginally-severe thunderstorms affected Gosper and Furnas counties during the evening hours of September 15th. A weak upper level shortwave along with a surface trough combined with moderate instability and abundant moisture to spark off clusters of thunderstorms during the late afternoon and early evening hours. The strongest storms impacted portions of Gosper and Furnas Counties between 6-8 PM CDT, with localized instances of penny to nickel size hail reported. A lone severe wind gust of 65 MPH was also reported. While instability was moderate and moisture was plentiful, weak deep layer wind shear of only 20 knots or less likely precluded a greater, or more widespread, severe weather threat. Scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms continued well into the late evening hours, but thunderstorm intensity greatly decreased with loss of daytime heating.
episodes.173265: A thunderstorm was occasionally severe as it crossed Bennett and Todd Counties. The storm produced some large hail and wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.173266: A strong thunderstorm developed and tracked across eastern portions of Jackson County. Nickel sized hail was reported southeast of Interior.
episodes.173280: Thunderstorms developed in the Nebraska Panhandle during the late afternoon hours of September 16th. Storms initiated along a surface trough of low pressure. As storms tracked east, they encountered decent low level moisture and ample wind shear. This led to the development of severe storms across the area. Hail up to ping pong ball size and wind gusts to 65 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.173296: A surface front was across central FL with high pressure northeast of the region. Low level ENE flow was over the local area with higher-than-normal moisture across NE FL south of the I-10 corridor streaming showers and isolated storms over the local area. SW flow aloft under low level created back-building cells.
episodes.173695: An active pattern in mid-September resulted in several reports of flash flooding in southern Utah, in addition to some isolated thunderstorm related wind gusts in northern Utah.
episodes.174103: On September 15th, a cold front passed through northwestern Kansas allowing for thunderstorms to develop in the region during the evening hours. One of these thunderstorms produced a wind gust of 62 mph.
episodes.174574: A weak short wave trough moved across a marginally unstable atmosphere.  A weak surface boundary and lifting from the weak short waved helped to initiate a few severe thunderstorms.
episodes.174641: Funnel cloud reported near Lake Josephine in Highlands County.
